reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent (Claude), independent context — audited the SQL-injection surface (clean: allowlisted columns, bound values, validated table name, %d limit), memq parity, money-int64, NULL handling; empirically confirmed the empty-GroupBy distinct-count divergence

accepted on inspection — the HIGH distinct-count divergence was empirically demonstrated by the reviewer (SQL 3 vs memq 1) and the fix is verified by the new parity case; the others are a documented parity gap (kind), a name-sort tiebreak, and test coverage

records.finding: Empty-GroupBy distinct count returned the matching row count (SELECT 1 -> COUNT(*)=3) instead of 1, breaking memq parity.
records.evidence: inner := "SELECT 1"; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM tbl WHERE ...) = row count; memq canonicalizes the empty key -> len(seen)==1
records.reason: Empty case now uses SELECT DISTINCT 1 (collapses matching rows to one -> COUNT 1, or 0 if none), matching memq. New parity case asserts it.

records.finding: The allowlist omitted the 'kind' label that memq exposes, an undisclosed parity gap (group/filter by kind errored here, worked in memq).
records.evidence: memq.eventLabels includes 'kind'; labelColumns had no kind
records.reason: Added a kind column to the documented schema, the allowlist, and the test seed; parity case group-by [currency,kind] added.

records.finding: Ordered multi-key ties broke by GroupBy order while memq tiebreaks by canonical (label name sorted), so a Limit could keep a different set.
records.evidence: orderClause appended cols in GroupBy order vs memq canonical() name-sorted
records.reason: tiebreakCols now sorts group labels by name and maps to columns, matching memq's canonical tiebreak; ordered multi-key parity case added.

records.finding: The parity test omitted empty-GroupBy distinct_count (the bug), OrderCountDesc, and ordered multi-key — the divergence paths.
records.evidence: the four original queries covered none of these
records.reason: Added parity cases for empty-GroupBy distinct_count, OrderCountDesc+Limit, ordered multi-key (segment,customer), and kind grouping.
